reason: Muscle needs usable energy, so I’ll start by bringing fuel and oxygen to the mitochondria.
expectation: I expect a stage of energy production that can help make ATP, though I’m unsure whether ATP will be made immediately.

alternatives.reason: The filaments seem relevant to pulling, but I want to establish the energy supply first.

effect: The result shows glucose is first split in the cell fluid before smaller fuel molecules enter the mitochondrion, so I’ll continue toward ATP production.
reaction: The split before mitochondrial entry was a useful detail.
reason: Combining ADP and phosphate with the fuelled mitochondria seems like the next step toward usable energy.
expectation: I expect ATP to be produced, though I’m unsure how the result will represent it.

alternatives.reason: The filaments are needed for pulling, but I want to finish the energy supply first.

effect: The ATP supply shows energy moving to the pulling machinery while ADP and phosphate return, so I can now build that machinery.
reaction: The recycling loop helps connect fuel use to ongoing muscle work.
reason: The thin and thick filaments appear to be the parts that produce the pull.
expectation: I expect them to form the fibre’s pulling machinery, though it may need other components to work.

alternatives.reason: Combining the cell with the fibre structures also seems necessary, but I want to assemble the pulling parts first.

effect: The overlapping filaments form units that can become part of the muscle fibre, so I’ll assemble the fibre next.
reaction: The overlap makes the arrangement clearer, though it has not yet shown how pulling works.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it appears to connect the cell to its muscle fibre structures.
expectation: I expect a more complete muscle fibre that can later incorporate the sliding filament units.

effect: The muscle fibre provides spaces for the sliding filament units, so I can now fit them together.
reaction: The scaffold makes their relationship clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it places the pulling units inside the fibre.
expectation: I expect a muscle fibre containing the filament units, though it may still need energy and a calcium signal to pull.

effect: The filament units are now inside the muscle fibre, ready to be connected to its energy supply.
reaction: The assembly is clear, though the result is predictable.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and ATP should supply energy for the fibre’s work.
expectation: I expect an energy-supplied muscle fibre that may still need a calcium signal to pull.

effect: ATP lets the myosin head release and reset, while the thin filament’s binding site remains covered; the calcium signal may change that.
reaction: The close-up makes ATP’s role more specific than simply supplying energy.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and calcium appears to be the next signal needed for pulling.
expectation: I expect calcium to uncover the binding site and allow the filaments to pull, though I’m unsure whether relaxation will follow immediately.

effect: Calcium uncovers the grip sites, allowing repeated myosin pulls that slide the filaments together; the fibre now needs to relax.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments staying the same length is clear and useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the calcium pumps appear relevant to ending the signal and allowing relaxation.
expectation: I expect the pumps to move calcium back into storage so the binding sites become covered and the fibre can relax.

effect: Calcium pumps use ATP to restore calcium to storage after the signal ends, covering the grip sites and stopping the pull. The fibre relaxes under an outside pull and is ready to respond again.
reaction: It was useful to see that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the calcium signal was most worthwhile: the result connected the signal to myosin pulling and clearly distinguished fibre shortening from filament shortening.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the fibre scaffold and then filling it felt predictable, especially with only one combination offered at each step.

surprise.text: ATP binding makes myosin release, and splitting ATP resets the head. That gave me a more specific understanding of its role in muscle work.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the sequential assembly choices left little room for decisions once the energy supply and filaments were made.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the fibre becomes part of a larger body system, though I hope for more meaningful choices.
